alt: Four explanations surround the partition of Africa: economic motives, strategic rivalry over the route to India, nationalism and prestige, and technology such as quinine, steamships and the machine gun. They lead to the Berlin Conference of 1884-85, which set the rule of effective occupation; by 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia were independent.
caption: Explanations combine motive and means; the Berlin Conference set the rules for claims.

alt: Five cases of African response on a time scale from 1880 to 1910. The Mahdist state lasted from 1885 until defeat at Omdurman in 1898; Samori Touré resisted France until captured in 1898; the Herero and Nama were destroyed in 1904-08; Maji Maji in 1905-07 was suppressed. Only Ethiopia, after victory at Adwa on 1 March 1896, preserved its independence.
caption: Most resistance was crushed; Ethiopia at Adwa is the exception to explain.

alt: A bar from 1899 to 1994 split to scale into the five periods 1899-1910, 1910-48, 1948-60, 1960-76 and 1976-94. Key dates hang below, from the Natives Land Act of 1913 and the National Party victory of 1948 to Sharpeville in 1960, Soweto in 1976, Mandela's release in 1990 and the elections of 27 April 1994.
caption: Apartheid had phases: learn which laws and protests belong to which.

alt: Four factor cards, internal resistance, economic pressure, the end of the Cold War and the decisions of de Klerk and Mandela, each with an arrow into one box: apartheid ends, from Mandela's release on 11 February 1990 to the elections of 27 April 1994.
caption: No single factor ended apartheid: weigh all four.

after: ## Content area 3: the Middle East after 1945
alt: A vertical timeline from 1948 to 1981. Gold dots mark the four wars: 1948 (after Israel was declared on 14 May), 1956 (the Suez crisis after Nasser nationalized the canal company), the Six-Day War of June 1967 and the October 1973 war followed by the oil embargo. Other entries: the Free Officers' coup of 1952, the United Arab Republic of 1958-61, Camp David in 1978, the peace treaty of 1979 and Sadat's assassination in 1981.
caption: Four wars, four sets of causes and results: 1948, 1956, 1967, 1973.

after: ## Content area 3: the Middle East after 1945
alt: A vertical timeline of Iran: Mosaddegh nationalizes oil in 1951 and is overthrown in a coup backed by Britain and the USA in 1953; the White Revolution from 1963; the single-party Rastakhiz system of 1975; economic crisis after 1975; mass protest in 1978; the Shah leaves in January 1979, Khomeini returns on 1 February and the Islamic Republic is established after a referendum that spring.
caption: Modernization, repression and economic crisis came before the revolution of 1978-79.

alt: An essay plan. A thesis banner says modernization was a necessary but not sufficient cause. Four numbered paragraphs of about 10 minutes each follow: modernization's effects (the named factor), then repression and exclusion, economic crisis, and leadership and ideology. The conclusion returns to the thesis and names the coalition of opposition groups as what made 1978-79 different.
caption: Test the named factor first, then weigh the alternatives against it.
